slides.title: Your RAG demo works. Production will *break* it.
slides.body: 7 failure modes I design for before a RAG system goes live, and the fix for each.

slides.title: The answer gets *split* in half
bullets: Fixed-size chunks cut tables, clauses and steps mid-way
Chunk by structure: headings, sections, table rows
Test recall on real user questions, not sample ones

slides.title: Vectors doing *math*
bullets: Similarity search finds similar words, not correct totals
Route metric questions to SQL on the live database
The database calculates. The model explains.

slides.title: The index goes *stale*
bullets: Source data changes, the vector index doesn't
Re-index incrementally with CDC or updated_at watermarks
Show 'last refreshed' next to every answer

slides.title: Retrieval ignores *who* is asking
bullets: One shared index means one user can see another's data
Filter by user and tenant at query time, never in the prompt
Mirror source permissions, e.g. row-level security

slides.title: More chunks, *worse* answers
bullets: Stuffing 20 chunks buries the one that matters
Retrieve wide, rerank, keep the top 3 to 5
Fewer tokens: lower cost, lower latency

slides.title: 'Looks fine' is not a *test*
bullets: Build a golden set of 50 to 100 real questions
Score retrieval and answers separately
Run it on every prompt, model or chunking change

slides.title: Failures nobody *sees*
bullets: Log the query, retrieved chunk ids, answer, latency, cost
When nothing relevant is found, say so instead of guessing
Review the lowest-scored answers every week

slides.title: Demo RAG answers. Production RAG knows when it *can't*.
